rowHint: Hide what you never use and move entries up or down within their group.
listHint: Opens when you right-click next to the files.
resetTip: Shows every entry again, in the usual order.
othersHintWindows: Everything CannonCommander has seen in the Windows menu so far. What you hide is gone the next time it opens.
othersHintLinux: Actions from Dolphin, Nemo, Nautilus and Thunar that CannonCommander has offered so far. What you hide is gone the next time it opens.
noneSeenTip: Open “Show more options” once and the entries will show up here.
propsWindowsTip: Security, details and previous versions in the Windows dialog.
propsSystemTip: Opens the dialog of your desktop's file manager.
iconsTip: Shows your system's icons throughout the list. Programs and shortcuts show their own icon even with this off.
iconsTipLinux: Shows your system's icons throughout the list. Programs and shortcuts show their own icon either way. CannonCommander only draws thumbnails in a sandbox. Where that isn't possible, as on Ubuntu 24.04, you only see the ones your file manager has already made.
thumbsTip: Ubuntu only lets a program into a sandbox with a permission of its own. Turning this on adds a small AppArmor rule for CannonCommander, which asks for your password, and after a restart it draws thumbnails itself. Turning it off removes the rule again right away.
thumbsOn: Done. CannonCommander draws thumbnails itself from now on.
thumbsOff: Turned off. The AppArmor rule is gone again.
thumbsStillOut: The rule is in place, but the sandbox still doesn't work, sorry.
thumbsOnRestart: The rule is in place. After a restart CannonCommander draws thumbnails itself.
thumbsOffRestart: The rule is gone. It's fully off after a restart.
